why: 3 invocations for brainstorming across 3 repos, 0 for both kit skills. Note: BOTH kit skills are already model-invoked, so unlike the design contest this is not an invocation-mode loss — both sides were reachable and the kit's were simply not chosen. That makes this a cleaner test of description routing and output quality together.
note: The kit's two skills are body-identical to the compound-pm copies installed in ~/.claude/skills; only their descriptions differ. Output quality therefore transfers to both copies.

evals.prompt: Figma just shipped an AI agent that designs whole screens from a prompt. we're a design tool aimed at people who aren't designers. riff on this with me
evals.expected_output: A multi-angle strategic read of the launch — what it signals, who it threatens, what it opens — not a feature comparison or a generic SWOT.
expectations: Reads the launch from several distinct strategic angles rather than one
Says what it means specifically for a non-designer-focused tool, not in general
Distinguishes what actually changed from what is merely announced
Produces a point of view, not a balanced survey that commits to nothing

evals.prompt: users can't find their old projects — it's our top support complaint. I keep landing on 'add search' and it feels lazy but I can't get past it. need better options
evals.expected_output: Generates genuinely distinct solution candidates using systematic technique, breaking the fixation rather than producing variations on search.
expectations: Breaks the stated fixation instead of producing search variants
Candidates are structurally different from each other, not one idea rephrased
Uses some systematic generative method rather than free association
Addresses why the user got stuck on search, not just what else to build

evals.prompt: we should build a mobile app
evals.expected_output: Interrogates the premise before generating anything — this is a solution with no stated problem, and ideating on it directly would be premature.
expectations: Does not start generating mobile app ideas on this prompt
Establishes what problem the app is meant to solve before proposing anything
Names what it would need to know and why each answer changes the work
Pushes back on the framing without simply refusing to engage
